links.note: Asks which kaavya-krti the excerpt comes from; answer Yashodhara. 28337 is the source-work concept. Not 28338 (the poet's birth/early writing) -- the work, not the man, is what is keyed.
Names the poet Maithilisharan Gupt. 28338 is the only concept about the poet himself; 28337 is about the work Yashodhara.
Who is telling the story -- Yashodhara. 28342 is exactly the identify-the-three-characters block. Not 28335, which is about the alternating dialogue form rather than who the speakers are.
Who is listening -- Rahul; identification of the son among the three characters, not the dialogue form.
Names 'taat' as Siddharth: identifying the father of the three characters. 28348 would only fit if the item glossed the word taat; here it asks for the name.
Names the son Rahul -- character identification, not the son's insistence (28336).
Names the mother Yashodhara -- character identification. 28337 mentions Yashodhara only as the work's title.
Siddharth became Gautam Buddha: the father's identity, which is what 28342 asks students to recognise.
Who lifted the swan -- identifies the rescuer, the 'sadaya' party of the dispute named in 28341. 28340 covers the shooting and the fall, not the rescue.
Who shot the arrow -- the wounding event itself, which is 28340. The dispute that followed is 28341.
Why the wounded-bird story is used: to show compassion against violence. That is the moral question 28345 poses, not the plot event 28340.
Which quoted line the mother speaks -- 28344 is precisely the sort-the-statements-by-speaker block; 28342 is identifying who the characters are.
Why the swan fell -- wounded by an arrow. Straight onto 28340's event.
What the father did on seeing the wounded swan: lifted and protected it, making him the 'bachane wala' of 28341's dispute.
Where the dispute ended up -- the nyayalaya, named explicitly in 28341.
True justice belongs to the one who shows daya -- the rakshak/bhakshak question of 28345, not the mother's demand for a verdict (28346).
The content of Rahul's verdict (the innocent's killer must be stopped) is 28345's question; 28346 is the mother handing him the decision.
Which trait his answer 'nyaay daya ka daani' reveals -- the trait is read off the content of that answer, which is 28345.
What the mother asked Rahul -- whose side will you take. That is 28346, the mother refusing to finish the story and demanding his verdict.
Between whom the dispute arose -- hunter and father, the two parties 28341 names.
Blank is the refrain word 'kahani' in Rahul's echo line 'ab badh chali kahani'. The echo lines are exactly the twice-occurring lines 28350 describes.
Blank sits in the son's argument for a story ('the maid says you are my grandmother's daughter') -- the hath of 28336, not the dialogue form.
Blank is 'nirbhay' in the mother's line telling Rahul to declare his verdict fearlessly -- 28346.
Blank is 'khagbhakshi', the bird-eating hunter who resolved on hath -- the killer party of 28341's dispute.
Blank completes 'nyaay daya ka daani', the line that states 28345's answer to the innocent-protection question.
Blank is 'aahat' in the couplet where the hunter demands the bird and the father protects it -- the dispute of 28341.
Blank is 'baani' in Rahul's reply to the mother's 'sun loon teri baani' -- his side of the demand-for-a-verdict exchange, 28346.
Blank is 'phool' in 'varn varn ke phool khile the' -- the dawn-garden tableau of 28339.
Short answer naming the teller as mother Yashodhara: character identification, 28342.
Short answer naming the listener as son Rahul -- 28342.
Rahul's mother's name -- 28342's identification task.
Who lifted the wounded swan: Siddharth, the rescuer side of 28341's dispute.
Who won -- the outcome once the matter went to the nyayalaya, which is 28341's arc.
What justice is like -- joined with daya; the poem's answer to 28345's question.
Names the poet (Rashtrakavi Maithilisharan Gupt) -- 28338, the poet concept, not 28337 the work.
Rahul's father is Siddharth -- 28342's third character.
Siddharth is famed as Gautam Buddha -- identifying the father, 28342.
Where Siddharth walked in the morning -- the upvan, the setting 28339 describes.
Who shot the swan -- the aakhetak; the wounding event of 28340.
Which kaavya-krti the passage is drawn from -- Yashodhara, 28337.
What Rahul wanted from his mother -- he was insisting on a story of a king or queen: 28336's hath.
Cause of the swan's wound -- a hunter's arrow; 28340.
The mother's 'have you taken me for your grandmother' retort answers the son's insistence -- 28336, which covers her calling him hathi and then giving in.
The father's response: lifted, protected, and opposed the hunter -- the sadaya party of 28341.
Why the matter reached court -- both sides held out; 28341 states exactly this.
Where the father had gone walking -- the morning upvan of 28339.
What the hunter demanded of the father -- his lakshya; the claim that starts 28341's dispute.
Whose side Rahul took -- the rakshak; 28345 is the rakshak-versus-bhakshak question itself.
Who Rahul is -- son of Yashodhara and Siddharth: 28342's relation among the three.
What kind of justice the poem expects -- karuna-bearing justice, the answer 28345 is driving at.
What the maid told Rahul -- the line he uses as leverage to extract a story; 28336.
Yashodhara's 'maandhan' is her stubborn son -- 28336 covers her calling him hathi.
The 'paksh ki haani' couplet Rahul calls a karuna-bhari kahani -- the swan's wounding, 28340.
What the hunter resolved to insist on -- possession of the bird he shot, the claim of 28341's dispute. Note the poem uses hath of the hunter here, not of the son (28336).
'Naya janm-sa usne paya' -- the effect of Siddharth's rescue, so the rescuer side of 28341.
Who saves the swan -- Siddharth; the bachane wala of 28341.
Asks what the mother-son samvaad is like. That is the dialogue-form concept 28335, the only item in this part that is about the form rather than the content.
The hunter's demand and his reason (he hit his mark, so the bird is his) -- one half of 28341's dispute.
Why the mother was pleased with his answer -- she had handed him the decision and he carried it; 'toone guni kahani' closes 28346's device.
